newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait Central Bank wants state role in economy cut.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Central Bank wants state role in economy cut.

text.p: Kuwait's Central Bank governor said in remarks published on Sunday the state should reduce its involvement in the economy in favour of the private sector.

"Efforts should be condensed to reduce government domination of economic activities and develop the appropriate environment to increase private sector contribution in pushing the wheel of economic growth," Sheikh Salem Abdul-Aziz al-Sabah said, quoted by the newspaper al-Rai al-Aam.
The government, which employs almost all Kuwaitis in the workforce, dominates the economy and runs the country's oil wealth, 10 percent of world proven reserves.

The dominating role of the government on economic activities caused "distortion to the structures of prices and wages," said Sheikh Salem. "That is a fundamental source of the general budget deficit."
Kuwait projects a 1.17 billion dinar deficit in the 1997/98 (July-June) proposed budget and 1.21 billion dinars for the current fiscal year.
